name: OpenTodo
description: Your tasks, your server. An open-source, local-first task manager you can host yourself. Everything you expect from a commercial task app, without the subscription or the lock-in.

paragraphs: Plan your day, keep projects in order, set reminders and share lists with your family or your team. Works on your phone and your computer, even offline. No monthly plan per person, and your tasks stay with you.
If OpenTodo looks useful, a star on GitHub helps other people find it, and a coffee helps me keep building it.
features: No subscription, no lock-in. Free software under the AGPL. Nobody can paywall your task list or shut it down with the company.

Works offline, on every device. Each phone and computer keeps a full copy of your data (local-first), so the app works with no connection at all. The server syncs, backs up and shares; it is never in the way of an edit.

Your data, one folder. Everything lives in one /data volume around a single SQLite file. Export to JSON at any time, import it (or a CSV, or another app's export) on any instance, and schedule encrypted backups to disk,…

Tiny footprint. One container, one static binary of about 23 MB with the web app inside, around 20 MB of memory when idle. Runs on a Raspberry Pi or the cheapest VPS. No database server, no Redis, no mandatory…
Private by design. No telemetry, no analytics, no phone-home, no third-party scripts or fonts. The server only contacts what you configure (see Privacy).
